A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MoLF research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and matchable, including Appendices A–D retained in v2 and its added Appendix E.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic Eight-Gaussian experiments, HEST-1k human gene-expression prediction, zero-shot mouse melanoma evaluation, and architectural and guidance ablations.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results and adds evaluations of an eight-expert MoLF configuration in Tables 15–17.

M1.justification: Section 3.2.3 revises the specified auxiliary loss: v1 describes penalizing the coefficient of variation, whereas v2 specifies N times the dot product of average routing probabilities and assignment frequencies. The core VAE, conditional flow, routing, and inference remain unchanged. The PDFs do not establish whether this specification revision reflects an implementation change or a correction.

E1.justification: Both versions use conditional Eight Gaussians and HEST-1k for human HVG/Hallmark prediction and mouse melanoma transfer. The 1,386-gene panel is retained. v2 newly describes 29 training cancer-type labels, including unknown, without establishing expanded data coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain MLP, STPath, STFlow, STEM for HVG evaluation, and the existing dense and ablation comparators. Tables 15–17 reuse the relevant baseline sets; the addition varies MoLF's expert-count setting rather than introducing a distinct comparison method.

E3.justification: Appendix E adds evaluation of Top-2 routing with eight experts alongside the retained six-expert configuration. Original splits, metrics, training budgets, and guidance-selection procedures are unchanged. The newly specified training labels and unknown mouse cancer-type input disclose existing settings rather than establish changes to them.

E4.justification: New Appendix E tests sensitivity to increasing the expert count from six to eight on HVG prediction, Hallmark prediction, and mouse transfer. Existing MoE-removal, positional-encoding, gene-panel, guidance-scale, and expert-specialization analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations across two independent training splits. The added configuration follows the existing reporting format; no new seed counts, repeated-run protocol, confidence intervals, or significance tests are introduced.

E6.justification: Original numerical results remain unchanged. Tables 15–17 add eight-expert results: average HVG PCC 0.373, Hallmark PCC 0.174, and mouse PCC 0.205, alongside retained six-expert values of 0.382, 0.185, and 0.202. These are additional configuration results, not revisions of the original model's performance.

T1.justification: v2 adds formal definitions of routing probabilities, batch-average probabilities, assignment frequencies, and the auxiliary dot-product loss in Section 3.2.3, including Equations 10–12. This mathematically specifies a different penalty from v1's coefficient-of-variation description. Other derivations are retained; no new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions and claims: latent flow matching with expert specialization, superior pan-cancer prediction, and cross-species generalization through conserved morphological signals. Additional sensitivity evidence does not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: Appendix E newly interprets the expert-count comparison as supporting a robust six-expert design and resilience to moderate configuration changes. Existing biological mechanism explanations, spatial-context interpretations, and the limitation concerning experts' implicit morphological meanings remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 specifies training on a single A100 GPU, 29 training cancer-type labels including unknown, and use of the unknown label for mouse inference. Appendix B replaces the promise of code upon acceptance with a reported availability statement and repository link. The auxiliary-loss computation is also documented explicitly.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive related-work positioning are unchanged. Both versions retain the same distinctions from deterministic regression, STEM, STFlow, and STPath; Fedus et al. was already cited for load balancing.

P1.justification: v2 expands the load-balancing explanation, adds a short Appendix E and several implementation sentences, revises the code-access wording, removes the acknowledgment section, and updates the publication footer. Most prose and the main section sequence are retained.

P2.justification: v2 adds Tables 15–17, which redisplay existing comparisons with an additional expert-count configuration. Existing tables and figures undergo limited relocation and reflow, and Figure 3's caption is reworded. All eight figure graphics are retained without substantive visual changes.

improvement.justification: v2 provides limited but useful support for the expert-count choice through Tables 15–17 and improves reproducibility documentation through hardware, conditioning, and code-access disclosures. The new results show modest configuration sensitivity rather than a general performance improvement. The auxiliary loss is more explicit, although its relationship to v1's different description remains unresolved. Overall, these additions improve transparency and evidential support without substantially changing the paper.
